title: My Favorite "Anabolic Herbs" for Bodybuilding
summary: NH says most supplements are a scam, then recommends two herbs he eats regularly: raw garlic (immunity, blood pressure, cholesterol, pumps, steady energy) and raw or pickled ginger (insulin sensitivity, appetite, focus). He covers dosing, timing, how to prepare them, how to pick good ones, and downsides like smell and digestive upset.
claims: Most supplements are useless for bodybuilding; you don't need hundreds of dollars of powders and pills to build muscle
Natural bodybuilding is also about health and a long life, not only muscle
Raw garlic boosts the immune system, so you get sick less and miss fewer workouts, avoiding the regression that follows a flu
Garlic supplementation has been shown to lower blood pressure naturally
Better blood flow from healthy arteries delivers more nutrients to muscle and so helps recovery, so even young lifters benefit from starting garlic early
Garlic lowers LDL cholesterol while keeping HDL intact, useful for lifters who eat lots of eggs and animal products
Garlic acts as an antibiotic that kills bad gut bacteria and candida while sparing beneficial flora, unlike pharmaceutical antibiotics that wipe out the gut and cost you gym performance
He has eaten raw garlic non-stop for years and had zero stomach issues or parasites
Microplastic and chemical fears are mostly overblown excuses from men who want to justify TRT, though some is true: filter water with a carbon filter and eat raw garlic
Test boosters and similar products are nonsense marketing; nothing natural raises testosterone or simply makes muscles bigger
Raw garlic gives big pumps through better blood flow (nitric oxide); the effect lessens with habituation but stays as a constant improved circulation
Garlic gives a sustained stimulant effect through the day, cheaper and healthier than pre-workouts that spike and crash
Never eat a whole bulb; one to two cloves is enough and more will make you vomit and lose the effect
Downsides of garlic: breath and body odour, sweat smelling of garlic, gas, stomach pain and heartburn; some people simply cannot digest it
Start with half a clove, always with a meal, never on an empty stomach, twice a week
Target dose is one to two cloves every other day; studies show one clove per 24 hours maximises allicin benefits
He personally eats a whole bulb over four days, half every two days, because he digests it easily and loves the taste
Eat garlic at lunch, not before bed, to avoid heartburn; evening trainees will feel the effect during their session
Always eat garlic raw; cooking destroys allicin
Slice garlic very thin, let it rest 60 seconds (the 10-minute rule is a myth), and chew thoroughly to avoid stomach pain
Buy organic garlic; good garlic smells strongly at the root, is hard like wood, and has no sprouts
He started eating ginger a year and a half ago to complement garlic
Ginger extract reduces waist-to-hip ratio in obese patients, may help arthritis and joint pain, improves insulin sensitivity, aids digestion and may lower heart disease, cancer and Alzheimer's risk
Good insulin sensitivity shows as a pump and fuller muscles after carbs; since eating ginger he gets full muscles after rice or pasta instead of lethargy and brain fog
Eating a few pieces of raw ginger before bed makes low-appetite people wake up hungry, helpful when bulking
Ginger improves mental focus, better than nootropic brain pills, but does not give garlic's energy boost
Both garlic and ginger boost libido, likely through improved blood flow
Ginger downsides: sour armpit odour and it can cause diarrhoea
Start ginger with a small piece every 48 hours; he now eats four to five sizeable pieces every 48 hours
He cycles the herbs: garlic on upper body days for pumps, ginger on lower body days when he eats more carbs, to fuel heavy squats and hinges
Buy ginger from Asian markets; it must be dry, hard, clean (no mould), smell strong, show yellow juicy flesh and little fibre when broken
Pickle peeled ginger chunks in fruit juice (cranberry, cherry, apple, pineapple, grape) at least four days, replacing the juice, or in honey with a little water for 10-15 days in the fridge
Don't buy garlic pills or store-bought pickled ginger; they lack the active compounds, so prepare the herbs yourself
